title: Guthrie supports House bill to increase national security and foreign aid funding
text:
Guthrie supports House bill to increase national security and foreign aid funding
Congressman Brett Guthrie announced on July 15 the House passage of H.R. 8595, the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act for 2027. The legislation would allocate $47.32 billion to strengthen the United States’ position internationally and enhance domestic safety.
“I’m proud to support this legislation, which puts America’s national security interests first, supports our allies, takes action to counter our adversaries, and stops the flow of deadly drugs like fentanyl from coming into our country,” said Congressman Guthrie. “This bill rightfully refocuses our nation’s foreign policy to bolster our standing on the world stage and reinforces President Trump’s foreign policy agenda.”
The bill includes $15.15 billion for operations at the Department of State and related agencies and commissions. It also provides $22.45 billion for global health initiatives, economic assistance, and humanitarian programs administered by both the Department of State and Treasury. An allocation of $1.66 billion is designated for International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement programs—an increase over fiscal year 2026 levels—to address issues such as fentanyl trafficking.
Additional provisions in H.R. 8595 redefine foreign assistance with a focus on promoting self-sufficiency abroad while supporting U.S. national security objectives. The act allocates $3.3 billion in Foreign Military Financing Program funds for Israel along with additional support for regional partners including Egypt and Jordan.
The legislation also aims to limit access by the Chinese Communist Party to U.S.-backed resources.
Brett Guthrie is currently serving in Congress representing Kentucky’s 2nd district after replacing Ron Lewis in 2009; he previously served in the Kentucky Senate from 2000 through 2008, according to official congressional records. Guthrie was born in Florence, Alabama in 1964 and now resides in Bowling Green.
